userStories.title: Define the authenticated chat ask file protocol
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the signed, atomic per-job file protocol shared by child plugins and the parent registry.

**Motivation** — `InteractionChain.receive` cascades only on a thrown error and Telegram resolves timeouts instead of throwing, so "chat first, Telegram later" cannot be built by registering two plugins; the chat plugin owns the fallback order itself.

**Approach** — All files live in one directory per job: `<outputDir>/chat-jobs/<jobId>.asks/` (helper `jobAsksDir(outputDir, jobId)` in `job-store.ts`), created with mode `0o700`. Every write is atomic (write a sibling temp file, then rename). `key` = the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the request id (`chatAskKey`), so any request id is a safe file name.

File content before authentication:
- `heartbeat.json`: `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "at": "<ISO time>" }` (parent).
- `<key>.ask.json`: `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "key", "request": <InteractionRequest>, "askedAt" }` (child).
- `<key>.answer.json`: `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "requestId", "action", "value"?, "respondedBy": "chat-user" | "chat-agent", "reason"?, "respondedAt" }` (parent).
- `<key>.settled.json`: `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "requestId", "by", "action", "value"?, "settledAt" }` (child).
- `<key>.notice.json`: `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "key", "request": <InteractionRequest>, "at" }` (child).

`by` in a settled record is the winning response's `respondedBy` (`chat-user`, `chat-agent`, the fallback plugin's value such as `telegram`), or `"timeout"`, or `"cancelled"`.

Answer encoding by request type (the same `InteractionResponse` vocabulary the chain already uses): `confirm` → `action` `"approve"` or `"reject"`; `choose` (including tool approvals) → `action` `"choose"`, `value` = the option key; `input` → `action` `"input"`, `value` = the text.

**Authentication (security review 2026-10-29).** The run's own agents can reach the ask directory, so a file's presence proves nothing. Every ask, answer, settled and notice record carries a `mac` field: lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed by a per-job 32-byte secret, over the record's JSON with the `mac` field removed and keys sorted (`signChatRecord(secret, record)` / `verifyChatRecord(secret, record)`, compared in constant time). Because the MAC covers `requestId`, an answer copied to another ask does not verify. Readers take the secret and treat a record with a missing or wrong `mac` exactly like a malformed one. The heartbeat is not signed (forging it can only delay the fallback). Bind answer requestId to the requested filename key as required by AC-23.

Constants: `CHAT_ASK_POLL_MS = 500` (child poll), `RUN_ASK_POLL_MS = 1_000` (parent tick, which also rewrites heartbeats), `CHAT_ASK_STALE_MS = 15_000` (a heartbeat older than this, or none, means the chat is closed). Export `CHAT_ASKS_FLAG = "--chat-asks"`.

**Scope** — In: new `src/interaction/chat-ask-files.ts`, record types, atomic writers/readers, heartbeat removal/freshness, notice consumption, `_chatAskFileDeps` for filesystem calls, exports from `src/interaction/index.ts`, temp-directory tests. Out: `jobAsksDir` and directory creation/secret delivery belong to US-008; plugin polling belongs to US-002–US-004. Signing the heartbeat file; forging it can only delay the fallback, never answer an ask. Pruning or deleting ask directories after a job ends.

**Interface** — `chatAskKey(requestId)`, `signChatRecord(secret, record)`, `verifyChatRecord(secret, record)`, `writeChatAsk(dir, request, now, secret)`, `readChatAsks(dir, secret)`, `writeChatAnswer(dir, key, answer, secret)`, `readChatAnswer(dir, key, secret)`, `writeChatSettled(dir, key, settled, secret)`, `readChatSettled(dir, key, secret)`, `writeChatNotice(dir, request, now, secret)`, `takeChatNotices(dir, secret)`, `writeChatHeartbeat(dir, now)`, `chatHeartbeatFresh(dir, nowMs)`, `removeChatHeartbeat(dir)`. Use the AC round-trip contracts for reader return values while retaining authenticated wire records.

userStories.title: Guard child answers and attribute agent approvals to the model
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Reject untrusted or forbidden child-side answers, define cancellation/errors and record model approval attribution.

**Motivation** — `initInteractionChain` returns null for headless + `cli` (`src/interaction/init.ts`), so a chat-launched run's tool approvals are denied `unavailable` and its triggers never reach a person.

**Approach** — F1: Child cannot write `<key>.ask.json` and has no fallback → `send` throws `NaxError` code `CHAT_ASK_WRITE_FAILED` (the existing callers already treat a thrown send as unavailable). F3: `<key>.answer.json` is malformed JSON or has an unknown `action` → ignored with one warning; the child keeps waiting. F15: A record's `mac` is missing or does not verify → treated as malformed: ignored with one warning per file. F7: A `chat-agent` answer names `allow-remember`, or answers a human-only ask → child downgrades `allow-remember` to `allow`; child ignores an agent answer to a human-only ask and keeps waiting. Human-only means `request.metadata.safety === "red"` or `request.metadata.trigger` is `"pre-merge"` or `"human-review"`.

`cancel(request.id)` while receiving resolves with `respondedBy: "timeout"` but writes settled `by: "cancelled"`; receiving an unsent id rejects with `CHAT_ASK_UNKNOWN`.

`decideSessionOutcome` (`src/interaction/ask-link-session.ts`). Target: when `response.respondedBy === "chat-agent"` the outcome carries `decidedBy: "model"` (an existing `AskDecidedBy` value, "an LLM decided"), for allow and deny alike, so the approval audit row records the agent. `deny()` accepts `"model"`. Other responses are unchanged.

**Scope** — In: extend ChatAskPlugin, `deny` and `decideSessionOutcome`, new guards tests with fake timers and signed/forged files, and regression assertions preserving human allow/deny attribution. Out: fallback (US-004), parent route policy/tool validation (US-012–US-014). Changing the approvals store `approvedBy` field; only the user can choose "allow-remember", so only human approvals are ever remembered. The chat agent remembering an approval ("allow-remember"); only the user may choose it on a card.

**Interface** — Existing `ChatAskPlugin.send(request)`, `receive(requestId, timeout)`, `cancel(requestId)`, and `decideSessionOutcome(response, req, onRemember)` keep their caller contracts; extend `deny`'s decidedBy input union with `"model"`.

userStories.title: Select the chat chain and parse the hidden directory and secret
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend interaction initialization to select ChatAskPlugin and add reusable absolute-path and stdin-secret parsing.

**Motivation** — `initInteractionChain` returns null for headless + `cli` (`src/interaction/init.ts`), so a chat-launched run's tool approvals are denied `unavailable` and its triggers never reach a person.

**Approach** — A hidden `--chat-asks <dir>` flag (constant `CHAT_ASKS_FLAG`) names the job's ask directory. When it is present, `initInteractionChain` builds a chain whose single plugin is `ChatAskPlugin` (name `"chat"`), even in headless + `cli`. `ChatAskPlugin` wraps the plugin the project config names as its fallback when that plugin is not `cli` (Telegram or webhook); with `cli` there is no fallback. Every ask source already goes through the chain or its primary plugin, so nothing upstream changes. A flag, not an environment variable: an env var would be inherited by any nested `nax` the run's own agents start.

`chatAsksDir` without `chatAskSecret` logs a warning and builds the chain as if no ask directory was given; plugin construction goes through a new `_interactionInitDeps.createInteractionPlugin`.

`ChatAskPlugin` has no `init` of its own. `InteractionChain.init` looks configs up by plugin name (`"chat"`), so `initInteractionChain` calls `fallback.init(config.interaction.config ?? {})` itself before constructing the plugin, and registers the chat plugin without calling `chain.init`. Pass `config.interaction.defaults.chatAskFallbackMs` as fallbackDelayMs.

The child reads that one line at start (`readChatAskSecret(stream, CHAT_ASK_SECRET_READ_MS)`, 5 000 ms) before building its chain. F14: The child reads no valid secret line within `CHAT_ASK_SECRET_READ_MS` (empty, not 64 hex characters, or timeout) → warning; the chain is built without the chat plugin (as without `--chat-asks`). F12: `--chat-asks` value is not an absolute path → `nax run` exits with "--chat-asks must be an absolute path"; `nax bot` prints it and exits 1. This story supplies the parser; callers integrate exits in US-006/US-007.

**Scope** — In: init options/dependency seam and new `src/cli/run-chat-asks.ts` modeled on run-max-iterations, unit tests with streamed valid/invalid/timeout secret cases. Out: CLI action wiring (US-006/US-007), parent secret generation (US-008). Runs and bot jobs not launched from `nax chat`: without `--chat-asks` their interaction chain is built exactly as today. Changing `InteractionChain` cascade semantics or registering more than one plugin in a chain. US-005 only: a config with no `interaction` section; the schema always supplies one, and `initInteractionChain` keeps returning `null` for it.

**Interface** —
```ts
initInteractionChain(config, headless, options?: { readonly chatAsksDir?: string; readonly chatAskSecret?: Uint8Array })
```
`parseChatAsksFlag(undefined)` returns `{ ok: true, value: undefined }`; an absolute path returns `{ ok: true, value: path }`; an invalid relative value returns `{ ok: false, message: "--chat-asks must be an absolute path" }`. `readChatAskSecret(stream, CHAT_ASK_SECRET_READ_MS)` returns a 32-byte Uint8Array or undefined; never use argv, disk or environment to carry the secret.

userStories.title: Thread nax run's hidden chat ask option through setup
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry the hidden run flag and memory-only secret from the CLI to setupRun's injected interaction initializer.

**Motivation** — `initInteractionChain` returns null for headless + `cli` (`src/interaction/init.ts`), so a chat-launched run's tool approvals are denied `unavailable` and its triggers never reach a person.

**Approach** — `RunSetupOptions.chatAsksDir?: string`; calls `_runSetupDeps.initInteractionChain(config, headless, chatAsksDir ? { chatAsksDir, chatAskSecret } : undefined)`. `RunOptions` (`src/execution/runner.ts`), `RunnerSetupOptions` (`src/execution/runner-setup.ts`) and the run CLI options (`bin/run-action.ts`, `bin/run-action-execute.ts`, `bin/nax.ts`) carry `chatAsksDir` the same way they carry `headless`. The option is declared as `new Option("--chat-asks <dir>").hideHelp()`; the run action validates it with `parseChatAsksFlag` beside `parseMaxIterationsFlag` and on failure prints the message and exits 1, as that flag does. When the flag is present the action reads the secret with `readChatAskSecret(process.stdin, CHAT_ASK_SECRET_READ_MS)` and passes `chatAskSecret` down the same path as `chatAsksDir`; the bot commands do the same in `withBotInput` (US-007).

The CLI → `run()` hand-off is plain property passing like `headless` and is held by the type checker; the ACs pin the `setupRun` and `runSetupPhase` end. Add chatAsks to the current CLI options shape (named RunActionOptions in this checkout), and chatAsksDir/chatAskSecret to RunOptions, RunnerSetupOptions and RunSetupOptions, forwarding both through each explicit projection. Invalid/absent secrets retain US-005's warning and ordinary chain path, not a new exit behavior.

**Scope** — In: bin/nax.ts, bin/run-action.ts, bin/run-action-execute.ts, src/execution/runner.ts, src/execution/runner-setup.ts, src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup.ts and real-setup seam tests, including propagation of interaction-init errors through the existing setup failure path without swallowing them. Out: bot wiring (US-007), runner launch argv/secret creation (US-008). Pipeline mode. US-006 only: an executable test of the `nax run` action exiting on a bad `--chat-asks`; `bin/run-action.ts` calls `process.exit` and is not unit-tested, as with `--max-iterations`. The parse is pinned through `parseChatAsksFlag`.

**Interface** — Add `chatAsks?: string` to the CLI options and `chatAsksDir?: string` / `chatAskSecret?: Uint8Array` along the run/setup options path. `_runSetupDeps.initInteractionChain` must receive an explicit undefined third argument when no directory is supplied. Preserve the returned chain as setupRun's interactionChain.

[integration] setupRun without chatAsksDir calls _runSetupDeps.initInteractionChain with (config, headless, undefined).

[integration] runSetupPhase given chatAsksDir: "/tmp/asks" and chatAskSecret: secret reaches _runSetupDeps.initInteractionChain with { chatAsksDir: "/tmp/asks", chatAskSecret: secret } as the third argument.

userStories.title: Give chat-launched bot review and fix steps an interaction chain
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Parse the hidden bot flag and secret, attach a chat chain to review/fix contexts and destroy it when each step ends.

**Motivation** — Bot review / fix pass no `interactionChain` to `buildPrStepContext`.

**Approach** — `_botReviewDeps` is defined in `src/bot/review-deps.ts` and re-exported by `review-run.ts`; `_botFixDeps` (`src/bot/fix-run.ts`) copies members of it by value at load. Target: `initInteractionChain` is a member of both `_botReviewDeps` and `_botFixDeps`, so a test stubs each one separately.

Bot inputs (`src/bot/review-run.ts`, `src/bot/fix-run.ts`, `src/cli/bot.ts`). Target: `chatAsksDir?: string` on both inputs; when set, the chain from `initInteractionChain(config, true, { chatAsksDir, chatAskSecret })` is passed as `interactionChain` and destroyed when the step ends.

The hidden option on both bot commands, validation in `withBotInput` through `parseChatAsksFlag` and the secret read with `readChatAskSecret`, `chatAsksDir` and `chatAskSecret` on `BotReviewInput` / `BotFixInput` (passed through `runBotFixCycle` by its existing input spread), `initInteractionChain` added to `_botReviewDeps` (`src/bot/review-deps.ts`) and to `_botFixDeps`, building and destroying the chain in `reviewCheckout` and the fix step, and F8.

F8: Bot job: `initInteractionChain` throws for the ask directory → warning; the bot step runs without a chain (today's behaviour). F12: `--chat-asks` value is not an absolute path → `nax run` exits with "--chat-asks must be an absolute path"; `nax bot` prints it and exits 1. Register both options as `new Option("--chat-asks <dir>").hideHelp()`. Read a secret line only when the flag is present, before chain construction; invalid secret uses the original chain path according to US-005. Omit interactionChain/chatAsksDir keys entirely when absent as the ACs require. Use finally for chain destruction on success, exceptions and early returns.

**Scope** — In: bot CLI types/deps/registration/shared parsing, both bot input types and lifecycle/deps, new bot seam tests and existing test/unit/cli/bot-review.test.ts cases; verify existing fix-cycle spread propagation. Out: run CLI wiring (US-006), job runner changes (US-008), changing bot trust/checkout/forge policy. Runs and bot jobs not launched from `nax chat`: without `--chat-asks` their interaction chain is built exactly as today.

**Interface** — `BotReviewInput` and `BotFixInput` gain `readonly chatAsksDir?: string` and `readonly chatAskSecret?: Uint8Array`; both bot dependency objects expose `initInteractionChain(config, true, { chatAsksDir, chatAskSecret })`; withBotInput handles raw `chatAsks?: string` and stdin reading through a testable seam.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Prepare eligible detached jobs' ask transport before spawn and send each secret only through stdin.

**Motivation** — Slice 2 left this gap on purpose (`2026-10-27-nax-chat-workflow-dispatch-slice2-design.md` 4.6): the launch card warns "this run has no channel for its own asks; they will time out".

**Approach** — The job runner creates the ask directory and writes a first heartbeat before it spawns a `run`, `bot_review` or `bot_fix` job, and appends `--chat-asks <dir>` to the argv (never for `plan`).

`DetachedJobs.launch` (`src/chat/jobs/job-runner.ts`). Target: for `run`, `bot_review`, `bot_fix` generates a secret with a new `_jobRunnerDeps.randomSecret()`, spawns with `stdin: "pipe"` and writes the secret line to the child's stdin, then closes it (other kinds keep `stdin: "ignore"`); `ChatJobs` gains an optional member `askSecret?(id: string): Uint8Array | undefined` (optional so the existing hand-written `ChatJobs` fakes in tests still type-check), answered from memory for jobs this runner spawned; the secret is never written to the job record. It also calls a new `_jobRunnerDeps.createAsksDir(dir, now)` (creates the directory and writes the first heartbeat, in one try block) and spawns `[...request.argv, CHAT_ASKS_FLAG, dir]`; the record stores the spawned argv. The existing `_jobRunnerDeps.mkdir` keeps serving `jobsDir` only.

The secret never touches disk, argv or the environment: the job runner generates it (`_jobRunnerDeps.randomSecret()`), spawns the job with `stdin: "pipe"`, writes the secret as 64 hex characters plus `"\n"` and closes stdin; the child reads that one line at start (`readChatAskSecret(stream, CHAT_ASK_SECRET_READ_MS)`, 5 000 ms) before building its chain. Extend child/spawn types to represent stdin.write/end.

userStories.title: Report run ask outcomes and close registry resources safely
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fill transcript notes, authentication diagnostics, job-end aborts and full registry disposal.

**Motivation** — Slice 2 left this gap on purpose (`2026-10-27-nax-chat-workflow-dispatch-slice2-design.md` 4.6): the launch card warns "this run has no channel for its own asks; they will time out".

**Approach** — `takeNotes()` returns these exact lines (`<summary>` is the request's `summary`, `<answer>` is the response `value` when present, else its `action`):
`[<jobId>] ask settled by <by>: <answer>` (settled by a fallback plugin or the agent elsewhere),
`[<jobId>] ask timed out: <summary>`,
`[<jobId>] <summary>` (a notice file, for example an advisor heads-up),
`[<jobId>] agent answered <answer>: <reason>`,
`[<jobId>] could not deliver your answer for <askId>`.
An ask settled by `chat-user` (the user's own card), by `chat-agent` (the agent's own answer already produced its line) or by `cancelled` produces no line. US-013 produces the agent-answered line; implement all other queued lines here and drain once through takeNotes, notifying onChange when notes are queued.

When a job leaves `running` (ended, cancelled, lost), the registry aborts the signals of that job's open cards and writes no answer for them.

F10: Registry tick hits a read error in an ask directory → warning; that directory is skipped this tick and retried next tick. F11: Registry cannot write the user's answer file → transcript note "could not deliver your answer for <ask id>"; the child keeps waiting. F13: A job leaves `running` while one of its cards is open → the card's signal is aborted; no answer is written. F15: A record's `mac` is missing or does not verify → treated as malformed: ignored with one warning per file.

The parent keeps the secret in memory only (`ChatJobs.askSecret(id)`), so after a chat restart a re-attached job has no secret on the parent side: the registry neither refreshes its heartbeat nor reads its directory, the child sees the chat as closed, and its asks go to the fallback plugin and then the timeout default. Validate parent-side ask/notice/settled records through the file protocol and sign answers. Treat an absent optional jobs.askSecret method like an absent secret.

`dispose()` removing heartbeats and stopping the tick: remove managed running jobs' heartbeats, unsubscribe jobs changes, clear pending timer handles and abort open card signals. Ensure a tick or asynchronous card resolution already in flight cannot write after teardown. Do not remove ask directories.

**Scope** — In: extend run-asks.ts with notes, failure isolation, authentication/secret eligibility, job-state cancellation and disposal, new notes tests. Out: agent queue/streak (US-013), transcript rendering/host close composition (US-014). Chain approval or the ask secret surviving a chat restart; a re-attached job's asks go to the fallback plugin and then the timeout default. Pruning or deleting ask directories after a job ends.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fill the registry's agent route, bounded notice queue, answer validation and escalation to human cards.

**Motivation** — Slice 2 left this gap on purpose (`2026-10-27-nax-chat-workflow-dispatch-slice2-design.md` 4.6): the launch card warns "this run has no channel for its own asks; they will time out".

**Approach** — An agent-routed ask is queued as a notice (built by `buildRunAskNotice`) and delivered as a turn when the chat is idle, ahead of job and task notices. The agent answers with the no-card tool `nax-jobs__answer_ask` (`ask`, `answer`, `reason`) or answers `escalate`, which turns the ask into a human card. An agent answer applies once: `allow-remember` is refused for the agent. The answer shows as a transcript notice with the reason. US-014 supplies the tool and TUI delivery; this story supplies registry state.

The registry calls `routeRunAsk` for each new ask with `chainActive` from `chains.isActive(job.chainId)`: the agent notice queue (`peekNotice` / `takeNotice`), `answer`, `escalate`, the agent streak and `noteUserTurn`. An ask the agent escalated still counts toward `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_AGENT_ASKS`. If writing an agent answer fails, `answer` resolves `{ ok: false, message: "[chat] could not write the answer for <askId>" }`.

`routeRunAsk` returns `"human"` when any of: the job has no `chainId`; `chains.isActive(job.chainId)` is false (this also covers jobs re-attached after a chat restart, since chain state is session-local, although those jobs have no secret and never reach the registry anyway); `request.metadata.safety === "red"`; `request.metadata.trigger` is `"pre-merge"` or `"human-review"`; the agent has already been handed `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_AGENT_ASKS` (3) asks since the last user turn. Otherwise `"agent"`. The order does not matter: every condition yields `"human"` and only their absence yields `"agent"`. Increment on routing/hand-off, not successful answers; noteUserTurn resets.

`takeNotes()` agent-answer line is exactly `[<jobId>] agent answered <answer>: <reason>`. Encode confirm as approve/reject, choose as action choose/value option key, and input as action input/value free text; store respondedBy chat-agent and reason. Reject invalid options, allow-remember, stale/unknown/not-agent-waiting asks; return `{ ok: false, message: "[chat] ask <id> is not waiting for the agent" }` for the latter. Escalation removes a queued notice and opens the existing human-card path without writing an answer. Settlement elsewhere removes stale notices and invalidates answer eligibility.

**Scope** — In: extend existing registry and new run-asks-agent tests through real signed ask files and the tick. Out: route/builder implementation (US-012), provider tool and UI delivery (US-014). The chat agent remembering an approval ("allow-remember"); only the user may choose it on a card. Chain approval or the ask secret surviving a chat restart; a re-attached job's asks go to the fallback plugin and then the timeout default.

**Interface** —
```ts
export interface RunAskReply { readonly answer: string; readonly reason: string }
export type RunAskResult = { readonly ok: true } | { readonly ok: false; readonly message: string };
```
Fill `peekNotice(): string | undefined`, `takeNotice(): string | undefined`, `answer(askId: string, reply: RunAskReply): Promise<RunAskResult>` and `noteUserTurn(): void` on ChatRunAsks, retaining onChange/takeNotes/dispose contracts.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Compose the registry into real chat jobs, expose the no-card answer tool and deliver ask turns and transcript notes in the TUI.

**Motivation** — Slice 2 left this gap on purpose (`2026-10-27-nax-chat-workflow-dispatch-slice2-design.md` 4.6): the launch card warns "this run has no channel for its own asks; they will time out".

**Approach** — The tool in `createJobsProvider` (only when `runAsks` is supplied, appended after `chain_stop`), the provider's instructions calling `buildJobsInstructions({ answerAsks: true })` when `runAsks` is supplied, `createHostJobs` composing the registry and disposing it in `close()`, `ChatHost.runAsks`, `useJobs` delivering ask notices first and appending notes, `noteUserTurn`, and the two launch-warning texts in `src/chat/jobs/jobs-launch.ts` and `src/chat/jobs/chain-tools.ts`.

An agent-routed ask is queued as a notice (built by `buildRunAskNotice`) and delivered as a turn when the chat is idle, ahead of job and task notices. The agent answers with the no-card tool `nax-jobs__answer_ask` (`ask`, `answer`, `reason`) or answers `escalate`, which turns the ask into a human card. An agent answer applies once: `allow-remember` is refused for the agent. The answer shows as a transcript notice with the reason. Tool execution delegates to runAsks.answer, maps unsuccessful results to isError:true/content message, and never opens an approval card. Keep the existing tools/order and instructions exactly unchanged for providers without runAsks.

`createHostJobs` (`src/chat/jobs/jobs-host.ts`) returns `runAsks: ChatRunAsks` too; `createJobsProvider` options gain `runAsks?: ChatRunAsks`; `ChatHost` gains `readonly runAsks?: ChatRunAsks`; `useJobs` options gain `note: (text: string) => void`.

Subscribe to runAsks.onChange alongside existing notice sources, append takeNotes() lines through note as read-only transcript notices, prioritize peekNotice from runAsks before jobs and tasks, and consume it only after successful idle delivery. noteUserTurn resets the registry's agent streak as well as existing task-turn state. Keep failed deliveries queued.

Launch warnings (`src/chat/jobs/jobs-launch.ts`, `src/chat/jobs/chain-tools.ts`). Target text: "asks you do not answer in chat fall to the run's timeout defaults" and "run steps' asks you do not answer in chat fall to their timeout defaults", still only when `interactionPlugin === "cli"`.

Size caps: `src/chat/chat-host.ts` is 597 lines and `src/tui/chat/ChatApp.tsx` 600 against the 600-line source cap. Keep the run-asks logic in `src/chat/jobs/` and `src/tui/chat/use-jobs.ts`; the two capped files get only the field and the option wiring, offset by collapsing existing lines (for example the multi-line `useJobs` destructuring in `ChatApp.tsx`, and in `chat-host.ts` declaring `runAsks` beside `jobs` and assigning it in the existing `hostJobs` block) so each stays at or under 600 lines.

**Scope** — In: provider/host composition, required barrel exports, ChatHost field and wiring, useJobs/ChatApp option wiring, warning replacements, new tool/UI tests and existing host tests. Update test/unit/chat/chat-host-chain.test.ts AC-14 and AC-17 lists to append answer_ask after chain_stop; update test/unit/chat/jobs/jobs-launch.test.ts, jobs-launch-chain.test.ts and chain-tool-card.test.ts warning expectations, asserting the new warning is absent for telegram. Out: registry policy (US-010–US-013), child plugin/CLI work. koda and the ACP server: only the `nax chat` TUI host shows run-ask cards or delivers ask notices. The in-run advisor answering tool approvals or triggers; the advisor is unchanged. Pipeline mode.

**Interface** — `nax-jobs__answer_ask` requires string fields `ask`, `answer`, `reason` and calls `runAsks.answer(ask, { answer, reason })`. `createHostJobs` returns runAsks and disposes it in close(); ChatHost.runAsks is optional for compatibility; useJobs accepts note(text) without adding a second delivery loop.

routing.reasoning: No-card approval tool exposure and host lifecycle integration are security-sensitive; TUI scheduling and capped files add cross-module integration risk.

When answer_ask runs, the provider's approve callback is not called.

Repository exploration: codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this session, so discovery used direct Read, Grep and Glob tools rooted at /Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax. This is an enhancement entirely within packages/nax, not a new application or a cross-package API change. Follow packages/nax/AGENTS.md and docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:183 for the 600-line hard source cap, injectable external dependencies, cancellable timers, strict TypeScript, Bun runtime and bun:test. Architecture index docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:139 identifies workflow mode as the default and pipeline mode as frozen. Do not change package versions, permissions profiles or adapter packages. The supplied spec is authoritative: the checked-in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-29-nax-chat-run-asks-design.md:3 still labels itself an unapproved draft and contains older restart, directory-layout and approvedBy proposals (notably :164 and :232); implement the supplied signed .asks protocol and restart behavior instead, without reopening those decisions.

Existing child interaction contract: packages/nax/src/interaction/types.ts:17 defines InteractionRequest, :47 defines InteractionAction (approve, reject, choose, input, skip, abort), :50 defines InteractionResponse with numeric respondedAt, and :64 defines InteractionPlugin with optional init/cancel/destroy. Wire records use ISO timestamps and schemaVersion 1; convert to the existing response vocabulary at the plugin boundary rather than changing these read-only public types. packages/nax/src/interaction/init.ts:16 exports createInteractionPlugin and :49 exports initInteractionChain; its absent-interaction guard at :56 remains, and headless + cli returns null at :64. Existing non-chat behavior must be unchanged. Add _interactionInitDeps.createInteractionPlugin rather than mocking imports; configured non-cli fallback is explicitly initialized before wrapping because packages/nax/src/interaction/chain.ts:163 indexes config by plugin.name. The chat chain contains exactly one plugin; do not register fallback separately or call chain.init on the chat path. InteractionChain.receive at :87 cascades on exceptions only, while telegram receive/cancel at packages/nax/src/interaction/plugins/telegram.ts:234 and :253 resolve fabricated timeout responses. Therefore ChatAskPlugin must own concurrent chat/fallback arbitration, remaining-deadline calculation and cancellation, treating timeout/destroyed/superseded as absence rather than as a winning fallback answer. InteractionChain.prompt at packages/nax/src/interaction/chain.ts:126 maps choose value to the selected option key; preserve that behavior, including the allow option outside the nominal InteractionAction union. Defaults still belong to existing callers, not this transport.

Ask producers and approval audit: packages/nax/src/interaction/ask-link-session.ts:167 builds approval choose requests with allow, allow-remember and deny and metadata.approvalPrompt at :196; decideSessionOutcome at :207 currently classifies every non-timeout response as human, with deny's union at :101 excluding model. Change only attribution to model for chat-agent allow and deny; preserve timeout denial and the human remember path. Red-tier and pre-merge/human-review metadata must be enforced in the child as well as the parent, and agent allow-remember is downgraded to allow in the child and refused by the registry. Do not change the approvals store approvedBy contract. Existing InteractionRequest metadata is sufficient; no producer rewrites are required. The apparently headless-specific paused-story comment is misleading: packages/nax/src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup-init.ts:233 actually tests counts.paused > 0 && interactionChain !== null, so supplying a chain enables the existing prompt path without changing that module.

Run CLI plumbing: packages/nax/bin/nax.ts:236 declares headless and :263 calls parseRunPreconditionFlags; packages/nax/bin/run-action.ts:53 calls the shared options type RunActionOptions (the supplied spec also calls the CLI shape RunCliOptions), and :133 parses precondition flags with process.exit on invalid max iterations. Add the hidden chat option to the actual current options shape and parse through the extracted helper, not a new untested action harness. packages/nax/src/cli/run-max-iterations.ts:12 demonstrates discriminated parse results. packages/nax/bin/run-action-execute.ts:124 executes the single-agent path and :162 passes options to run; packages/nax/src/execution/runner.ts:114, :174 and :253 carry headless through RunOptions to _runnerDeps.runSetupPhase. packages/nax/src/execution/runner-setup.ts:15 declares RunnerSetupOptions and :69 explicitly projects fields into setupRun. packages/nax/src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup.ts:67 owns _runSetupDeps, :107 owns RunSetupOptions and :364 directly calls initInteractionChain today. Thread both chatAsksDir and chatAskSecret through every projection; add the seam there without moving resource/lock lifecycle logic. Use the real setup fixtures at packages/nax/test/unit/execution/lifecycle/run-setup-command-interceptor.test.ts:63 for the setupRun/runSetupPhase assertions. The action reads only one stdin secret line, only when the flag is present; malformed/absent/late secrets warn and fall back to the original chain path.

Bot plumbing: packages/nax/src/cli/bot.ts:9 defines injectable CLI deps, :39 BotReviewOptions, :60 withBotInput, :160 shared options registration and :174 both actions. Add hidden Option handling, absolute-path validation and injectable secret reading without making help load orchestration or blocking stdin when no flag exists. BotReviewInput is at packages/nax/src/bot/review-run.ts:46 and reviewCheckout starts at :411; BotFixInput is at packages/nax/src/bot/fix-run.ts:80 and fixCheckout at :352. Each loads the base config, creates runtime/context and disposes in finally. Build the chat chain only with chatAsksDir, pass it into buildPrStepContext, and destroy it exactly once even on failure or early refusal. packages/nax/src/bot/review-deps.ts:31 defines _botReviewDeps, re-exported by review-run; packages/nax/src/bot/fix-run.ts:37 copies its entries by value into _botFixDeps. Tests must stub both initInteractionChain entries separately. packages/nax/src/bot/fix-cycle.ts:30 and :49 already forward input and spread it to re-review/readiness, so added fields should propagate without a new transport. Chain-init failure warns and continues without an interactionChain key, not with an undefined field.

Parent jobs and storage: packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/job-types.ts:1 limits kinds to plan/run/bot_review/bot_fix, :5 defines persisted ChatJob with optional chainId/:24, and :34 defines safe JOB_ID_PATTERN. packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/job-store.ts:23 locates chat-jobs, :36 already uses sibling temp + rename for atomic publication, and :94 filters *.json so .asks directories are not job records. Mirror the dependency-injection/error conventions with _chatAskFileDeps, but do not store secrets in any JSON, path, log, argv or environment. The only new durable layout is <outputDir>/chat-jobs/<jobId>.asks/, mode 0700. Four record families are HMAC authenticated; heartbeat is intentionally unsigned. The answer reader must additionally bind requestId to its hashed filename, not merely verify MAC, so replaying a signed answer into another ask fails. Atomic publication, safe hashed names, schema/action validation, wrong/missing MAC rejection, one-warning-per-file and distinct absence versus unexpected I/O errors are key risks. Maintain enough diagnostic information for plugin/registry warnings even though public readers skip malformed records.

packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/job-runner.ts:30 defines ChatJobs; :57 defines OwnedChild without stdin, :62 restricts SpawnOptions.stdin to ignore, :122 owns spawn and :161 owns launch. Extend these types for a pipe and the secret write/end; askSecret stays optional for old handwritten ChatJobs fakes. Generate one per-job 32-byte secret, create asks directory plus first heartbeat before spawn in one failure boundary, append CHAT_ASKS_FLAG only on eligible successful setup, store the actual spawned argv, and keep ownership/secrets in memory only. Directory or heartbeat setup failure leaves a managed launch on original argv and adds the explicit asks-will-not-reach-chat note. Existing record-save failure management and no-retry warnings must survive. Attach at :348 never restores ownership or secret. Existing lifecycle tests at packages/nax/test/unit/chat/jobs/job-runner.test.ts:93 assert spawn/log ordering and original stdin/argv, and :122 assert immediate managed running state; preserve launch tracking semantics and adapt the explicitly changed argv/pipe expectations and clone test. Consider other spawn fakes in job-runner-attach/cancel and host-chain fixtures when changing OwnedChild typing; do not weaken unrelated process safety checks.

Parent cards and registry: packages/nax/src/chat/ask-controller.ts:4 already includes session question entries in ChatPendingAsk, :54 defines ChatAskController, :134 implements host-owned choices, :225 answers questions through the session only, and :235 resets host requests. Add a separate host-question waiter path with host-question- ids and null settlement on abort/timeout/reset, intercepting answerQuestion before session forwarding. Existing AskCard supports questions; no new widget is needed. Update the three handwritten UI fakes named by US-009. Registry is a new focused module under chat/jobs rather than host/UI monoliths. It authenticates/scans running owned jobs with secrets, refreshes heartbeat, deduplicates ask and settled processing, opens cards with abort signals, and guards late asynchronous completions from ended/cancelled/lost jobs. It must start on jobs.onChange, avoid overlapping ticks, use injected timeout/clock, unref timer handles when supported, and on dispose unsubscribe/clear/abort/remove owned heartbeats without deleting directories. Per-directory errors must not block other jobs. Full ChatRunAsks is declared in US-010 with placeholders, then US-011 and US-013 fill notes/security/agent members without changing consumers' interface. Parent answer records are signed. A parent restarted without the memory-only secret must not refresh heartbeats or inspect that directory; child fallback and its original timeout own recovery.

Agent routing and prompt boundary: packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/chain-controller.ts:38 already supplies ChatChains.isActive and :66 documents session-local chain state; :208 is the implementation. Route human unless chainId exists and is active, no red/human gate is present, and fewer than three asks have been handed to the agent since the user's last turn. Count escalation too and keep this counter separate from task notice turns. Job/key IDs identify outstanding asks. Prompt text belongs in prompts/builders, not registry literals: wrap summary, detail and option labels as untrusted data, escape internal closing tags, and put allowed answers/tool guidance outside the block. Agent tool validation and child revalidation are defense in depth. After foreign settlement, remove queued agent notices and reject stale answers. Transcript lines are exact spec strings; no duplicated lines for chat-user/chat-agent/cancelled settled markers.

Host/TUI composition and compatibility: packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-provider.ts:11 defines options and :97 builds four launch tools then list/cancel and optional chain tools; append answer_ask only with runAsks, after chain_stop when chains exist, with no approval card. packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-builder.ts:54 emits exactly eight existing guidance lines, re-exported at packages/nax/src/prompts/index.ts:134; add a ninth only on answerAsks:true. packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-host.ts:21 composes runner/chains/provider and :47 defines close; compose registry here, return it, and dispose it in close. packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts:74/:117 expose jobs, :157 composes hostJobs, :171 assigns jobs, and :558 closes hostJobs. It is 597 lines; only type/field/assignment/barrel wiring belongs here. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ChatApp.tsx is exactly 600 lines; :408 has a multiline useJobs destructure that can collapse to offset adding note. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/use-jobs.ts:7 owns hook options, :32 subscriptions, :47 idle delivery and :75 user-turn bookkeeping. Extend this focused hook to subscribe to runAsks, drain transcript notes through note(text), prioritize run-ask notices before job then bounded task notices, consume only after successful delivery, and reset both counters on user turns. Do not introduce a second send loop or duplicate autonomous turns. Launch-warning replacements occur at packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-launch.ts:182 and chain-tools.ts:135, still cli-only.
